text: This is Leverage. One frontier brain. An elastic workforce.

Your best model stays the strategist. Leverage is the intelligence resource manager underneath it: an MCP server with five tools that recruits local, free and subscription models, gives each one the smallest job it can verify, and replaces any that fail.

Point it at a repository and a model writes the plan. Set the budget to zero and paid routes are removed, not outranked. When a worker dies, its understanding is checkpointed and handed on. And nothing is called done until the repository's own tests say so.

The harness is a control plane. A goal compiles into a task graph. An auction scores every reachable model on fit, track record, cost and privacy. The winner runs as a RocketRide pipeline through a token gated pool. The test suite is the gate. A failure becomes a checkpoint, a replacement, and a resumed task.

The site is not a slideshow. Press one button and a real mission runs inside the deployment: a planner reads a repository with no plan at all, writes the task graph, the compiler validates it, workers are hired, every task passes its own tests, and the whole suite runs green. Credits read from billing, zero dollars paid.
Every mission is inspectable. The plan as the model wrote it. Each candidate's utility and the winner's reasoning. An append-only log. A proof pack with every check and its result.

And it lives where you already work. Added to Claude as a connector, one message points Leverage at a real repository: three guards for the failures at the top of the OWASP list. The plan arrives, the workers are hired, the tests pass, and the proof comes back into the chat.
Open the site. Press the button. Read the log. Leverage. Verified or nothing.
